excel-sheet-column-number.d: Convert an Excel column title (A, B, ..., Z, AA, AB, ...) into its column number.
excel-sheet-column-number.i: It's base-26 with digits 1..26: result = result * 26 + (c - 'A' + 1), scanning left to right.
k: Base-26 conversion from the right with powers

fibonacci-number.d: Return the nth Fibonacci number (F0 = 0, F1 = 1).
fibonacci-number.i: Plain recursion is O(2^n) because subproblems repeat. Iterate keeping only the last two values for O(n) time and O(1) space.

find-customer-referee.d: Return names of customers who were not referred by the customer with id 2 (including those not referred by anyone).
find-customer-referee.i: NULL != 2 evaluates to UNKNOWN, not TRUE, so you must add 'OR referee_id IS NULL' explicitly.

find-eventual-safe-states.d: In a directed graph, a node is safe if every path from it ends at a terminal node (no outgoing edges). Return all safe nodes, sorted.
find-eventual-safe-states.i: Reverse every edge; terminal nodes now have in-degree 0. Run Kahn's algorithm on the reversed graph: everything that gets removed can't reach a cycle, so it is safe.

find-first-and-last-position-of-element-.d: In a sorted array, return the first and last index of target, or [-1,-1]. Must be O(log n).
find-first-and-last-position-of-element-.i: Run binary search twice. When you hit target, record it and keep searching left (for first) or right (for last) instead of stopping.

find-median-from-data-stream.d: Design a structure that accepts numbers one at a time and can return the median of everything added so far.
find-median-from-data-stream.i: Two heaps: a max-heap for the smaller half and a min-heap for the larger half. Keep sizes within 1 and every element of 'small' <= every element of 'large'. The median is at the heap tops.

find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array.d: A sorted array of unique values was rotated. Find its minimum in O(log n).
find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array.i: At each step one half is sorted. If nums[lo] <= nums[mid], the left half is sorted: its minimum is nums[lo], so record it and search right. Otherwise the minimum is in the left part including mid.
k: Binary search on the sorted half, early exit if range sorted

find-peak-element.d: Return the index of any element strictly greater than its neighbours (outside the array counts as -infinity). Must be O(log n).
find-peak-element.i: If nums[mid] < nums[mid+1] you are on an uphill slope, so a peak must exist to the right; otherwise one exists at mid or to the left.
k: Binary search following the uphill side

find-special-substring-of-length-k.d: Is there a substring of length exactly k made of one repeated character whose neighbours (if any) are different characters?
find-special-substring-of-length-k.i: Equivalent to: some maximal run of equal characters has length exactly k. Scan runs in one pass. (Your version checks every window, O(n*k).)
k: Check each window of length k and its neighbours

find-the-duplicate-number.d: An array of n+1 integers in [1, n] has exactly one repeated value. Find it without modifying the array and with O(1) extra space.
find-the-duplicate-number.i: Treat i -> nums[i] as a linked list; the duplicate is where a cycle starts. Floyd: slow/fast meet inside the cycle, then reset one pointer to the start and move both one step until they meet.

find-the-index-of-the-first-occurrence-i.d: Return the index of the first occurrence of needle in haystack, or -1.
find-the-index-of-the-first-occurrence-i.i: Brute force compares needle at each start: O(n*m). KMP builds a prefix (LPS) table to get O(n+m). In an interview, know at least the brute force and the idea of KMP.
k: Brute force compare at each start

first-unique-character-in-a-string.d: Return the index of the first character that appears exactly once in s, or -1.
first-unique-character-in-a-string.i: Two passes: count frequencies (an int[26] is enough), then return the first index whose count is 1.

fizz-buzz.d: For 1..n output "FizzBuzz" if divisible by 15, "Fizz" if by 3, "Buzz" if by 5, else the number.
fizz-buzz.i: Check the combined case (3 and 5) first.

gas-station.d: Stations on a circle have gas[i] and it costs cost[i] to reach the next one. Return the start index that lets you complete the loop, or -1.
gas-station.i: If total gas < total cost, it's impossible. Otherwise scan with a running tank; whenever it goes negative, no station in the current stretch can be the start, so restart from i+1.
k: Total check + reset start when tank < 0

generate-parentheses.d: Generate all well-formed strings of n pairs of parentheses.
generate-parentheses.i: Backtrack on counts: add '(' while open < n, add ')' while close < open. Every string built this way is valid.

group-anagrams.d: Group the strings that are anagrams of each other.
group-anagrams.i: Anagrams share a canonical key: the sorted string, or the 26-letter count array. Map key -> list of strings.

hand-of-straights.d: Can the cards be split into groups of groupSize consecutive values?
hand-of-straights.i: The smallest remaining card must start a group. Count with a map, take the smallest key from a min-heap, consume first..first+size-1. If a count hits 0 out of order, fail.
k: Count map + min-heap of distinct values

happy-number.d: Repeatedly replace n by the sum of the squares of its digits. n is happy if this reaches 1; otherwise it loops forever.
happy-number.i: Either it reaches 1 or enters a cycle. Detect the cycle with a HashSet of seen values (or Floyd's slow/fast pointers for O(1) space).

house-robber.d: Houses in a row hold money; you can't rob two adjacent houses. Return the maximum you can rob.
house-robber.i: dp[i] = max(nums[i] + dp[i-2] (rob it), dp[i-1] (skip it)). Only the last two values are needed.
k: Bottom-up dp array from the right

house-robber-ii.d: House Robber where the houses form a circle, so the first and last are adjacent.
house-robber-ii.i: You can't take both the first and last house, so answer = max(rob(nums[0..n-2]), rob(nums[1..n-1])) using the linear House Robber.
